title: Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards Cardmember Agreement: Purchase Interest and the Grace Period
content:
**Method.** Purchase interest on a Marlowe & Finch Credit Cards account is computed by the average daily balance method (including new purchases) at the card's purchase APR divided by the card's days-in-year divisor for each day, and posts on the statement closing date.

**Grace period.** No purchase interest is charged in a billing period when the statement balance of the previous statement was paid in full by its payment due date (or was 0.00 or a credit).

**Disputed amounts.** Amounts under open billing dispute accrue no interest while the dispute is open, and none is charged afterward if the dispute is resolved in the cardmember's favor.

**Minimum interest charge.** When the interest computed for a period is above 0.00 but below the card's minimum interest charge, the minimum interest charge is charged instead, recorded as a minimum interest charge.

**Special financing.** Special financing purchases are governed by the special financing terms and accrue no purchase interest while their promotion runs.

## Outcomes by case (hypothetical periods; card minimum interest charge USD 2.00)

| Previous statement balance | Paid in full by its due date | Interest computed this period | Charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 600.00 | yes | — | no purchase interest |
| a credit of USD 20.00 | — | — | no purchase interest |
| USD 600.00 | no | USD 1.37 | USD 2.00, as a minimum interest charge |
| USD 600.00 | no | USD 14.20 | USD 14.20 purchase interest |
| USD 600.00 | no | USD 0.00 | nothing |

## Daily rate (hypothetical figures)

At a hypothetical APR of 36.50 percent and a divisor of 365, the daily periodic rate is 0.1 percent; an average daily balance of USD 1000.00 over a 30-day period gives USD 30.00 of purchase interest.
